{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOLEgSIs8AAAABZfzKEQ", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4Bm7fazhDG9ow", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4Bm7fa", "number": 39, "title": "Correct XRSession reference-space request conversion, identity and settlement", "body": "## Problem

At `dev` commit `02949f95ab31ba77355ba19f5a691c4a147e10a3`, `requestReferenceSpace()` checks session liveness before validating its argument, compares unconverted values, returns the cached `_viewer`, and lacks queued settlement. Non-viewer requests also perform another ended check after awaiting the adapter. Applications can observe rejected coercible arguments, shared viewer identities and inconsistent asynchronous behavior. `tests/conformance.ts` explicitly expects blanket ended-session rejection. See [current implementation](https://github.com/takahirox/WebXR-emulator-extension/blob/02949f95ab31ba77355ba19f5a691c4a147e10a3/src/polyfill/api/runtime.ts#L262).

## Expected outcome

Provide a correctly bound request operation that returns independently usable, session-owned reference spaces with consistent asynchronous behavior across Quest VR, Quest MR, Android AR and supported inline sessions.

## Context

Start from and target `dev`. Relevant files are `runtime.ts`, `geometry.ts`, `interface-brand.ts`, `session-init.ts`, `EmulatedXRDevice.ts`, `tests/conformance.ts`, and the Chromium/Firefox control helpers. The custom TypeScript API uses gl-matrix transforms and shared allocation brands; no polyfill dependency upgrade is needed.

Use [Device CRD 2026-06-09 §§4.1 and 6.2](https://www.w3.org/TR/2026/CRD-webxr-20260609/) and [WebIDL 622910c](https://github.com/whatwg/webidl/blob/622910c67c724e362f71e8255a0380bade261acb/index.bs). Existing capabilities grant `viewer` by default, plus `local` for immersive sessions. `local-floor`, `bounded-floor` and `unbounded` require negotiation. Current inline policy grants only `viewer`; Android has no immersive-vr mode.

Retain this requirement correction in the Issue/PR: **original assumption:** every request on an ended session must reject with InvalidStateError. **Correction:** the pinned Device request/support algorithms contain no general ended gate. Follow their support, allocation and settlement rules. **Rationale:** requesting a space does not reactivate presentation. [Chromium 156 source](https://github.com/chromium/chromium/blob/f842f52ef39fd97b449eb27cff414bf05a98ddce/third_party/blink/renderer/modules/xr/xr_session.cc#L837) does contain an ended gate and immediate resolution; record this divergence rather than overriding the agreed baseline.

All 38 existing Issues/PRs are closed. Earlier core work was explicitly partial; #21/#22 supplied bounded geometry, and #37/#38 established Firefox runtime. The [Firefox report](https://github.com/takahirox/WebXR-emulator-extension/blob/02949f95ab31ba77355ba19f5a691c4a147e10a3/docs/webxr-firefox-validation-2026-10-24.json) reports six application outcomes on Firefox 157.0; it does not establish these new contracts. Three.js r186 [awaits this operation during session startup](https://github.com/mrdoob/three.js/blob/9b4a2ac29c63ccb43fd51c5661f2f873ac2c39b8/src/renderers/webxr/WebXRManager.js#L526).

## Pre-merge acceptance

- [ ] Validate genuine XRSession receivers before argument conversion. Implement required-argument and enum ToString conversion once, before asynchronous work. Cover coercible objects/boxed strings, missing/null/undefined/invalid values, Symbols and thrown coercion values. Invalid receivers and conversion failures return rejected Promises; preserve rejection reasons. Include the operation's WebIDL property descriptor.
- [ ] Each successful call creates a fresh reference object, including repeated/concurrent viewer requests. Preserve the bounded subclass and session-relevant allocation realm, including borrowed methods across injected same-origin frames/popups.
- [ ] Queue successful creation/resolution and unsupported rejection as tasks. Test that these requests remain unsettled through the calling task's microtasks; distinguish binding failures. Avoid assertions about ordering between unrelated task sources.
- [ ] Preserve the stated profile/feature restrictions. Exercise every enabled immersive type, omitted optional features and valid-but-ungranted requests; the latter reject with NotSupportedError. Do not enable capabilities merely to make fixtures pass.
- [ ] Cover requests after end and requests pending when end occurs under the corrected contract. Every request settles once. Neither path restarts callbacks, presentation, input or disposed rendering resources. Keep unrelated ended-session checks intact.
- [ ] Demonstrate application-visible geometry: fresh viewer spaces follow virtual viewer movement, viewer-relative poses remain identity, independent offsets compose correctly, and fresh bounded spaces retain the authored polygon. Check foreign-session ownership and inactive-frame errors separately. Preserve existing local/floor origins and unbounded navigation.
- [ ] Add focused executable cases using the existing Chromium and Firefox extension/control routes, covering all three immersive configurations and inline on both device profiles. Add a focused entry/selector only if needed. Adapt applicable assertions from pinned WPT `xrSession_requestReferenceSpace`, `xrSession_requestReferenceSpace_features` and `xrSession_viewer_referenceSpace`; disclose native fake-device setup changes and the emulator's inline policy. Inspected test code is not a passing result.
- [ ] The Coordinator runs `npm run build:firefox` (including typecheck/build), the documented focused browser commands and `git diff --check`. Inspect generated bundle changes and record source/bundle provenance, exact browser/tool versions, outcomes, failures, skips and unperformed checks. Update the versioned API inventory. Tests and PR review remain Coordinator-owned; add no independent AI re-review or generic suite rerun.
- [ ] Correct further mistaken AI-authored requirements using retained original assumption, correction, pinned primary evidence and rationale in the Issue/PR, without human approval or independent AI re-review. Preserve meaningful acceptance and the fixed goal; do not relax requirements around unfinished code or failures.

## Optional validation

Run a focused startup scenario using the pinned Three.js manager to exercise its awaited reference-space request. Record actual results separately from existing application evidence.

## Required post-merge verification

None required.

## Specification reconciliation

This task was authored by AI under the agreed WebXR API compatibility goal for
Quest 3 VR/MR and Android AR. Correct erroneous technical assumptions or acceptance
criteria when primary specifications or measured evidence establish the correction.
Update this Issue and record the original
assumption, corrected requirement, primary reference and rationale in the PR.
These technical corrections require neither human approval nor an independent AI
re-review. Preserve the agreed goal and relevant pre-merge acceptance; do not weaken
requirements merely to accommodate incomplete implementation or failing tests.
